newsitem.title: UK: Dead and wounded in Russian-Chechen clash - report.
newsitem.headline: Dead and wounded in Russian-Chechen clash - report.

text.p: Russian police have clashed with a Chechen "gang" near the border with the separatist Chechnya region and there were casualties on both sides, Russia's Interfax news agency reported on Tuesday.

The agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted the commander of Russian forces in the North Caucasus, Partagen Andriyevskiy, as saying there were dead and wounded on both sides. No figures were given and the report did not say when the clash occurred.
The Chechens had crossed the border and were trying to make their way into the neighbouring region of Dagestan, Andriyevskiy said.
All crossing points on the Chechen border were being closed from 0200 GMT on Tuesday, he said, adding that troops all along the border were on full alert.
No independent confirmation of the clash was immediately available.
A powerful explosion tore apart a railway station in southern Russia on Monday, killing at least one person and injuring 17 in the second suspected bomb blast in five days.

Russian officials said they suspected Chechen separatists were behind the evening explosion at the station in Pyatigorsk, about 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Chechnya. Chechen leaders denied the charges.
Two people were killed in a bomb blast at Armavir railway station in southern Russia last Wednesday.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin said he was deeply concerned and made clear relations with the separatist leaders of Chechnya would deteriorate sharply if a Chechen link was confirmed and they did not crack down.

"The Interior Ministry and Federal Security Service leadership have enough forces and resources to take uncompromising actions and initiatives to stop terrorist acts," presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax.
The explosion in a first floor waiting room blew out all the windows and badly damaged the station in Pyatigorsk, which lies in the north Caucasus mountains.
The Emergencies Ministry said one person was killed and 17 were taken to hospital. Others had been slightly hurt but were able to walk and simply went home.
Russian news agencies quoted officials in Moscow as saying two people had been killed and up to about 15 hurt, but the reports were not confirmed by the Emergencies Ministry.

Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov told Itar-Tass news agency there were "Chechen links" and Federal Security Service (FSB) spokesman Alexander Zdanovich told Russia television that two suspects had been detained.
"There are signs that Chechen terrorists possibly took part in the explosion at the Pyatigorsk railway station," RIA news agency quoted Zdanovich as saying.
The Chechen leaders, who fought a nearly 21-month conflict with Russian troops over their demands for independence, denied any role in either blast.

"I categorically declare that the Chechen side did not take part in the terrorist acts on Russian territory," Chechen Vice President Vakha Arsanov told Ekho Moskvy radio station from the Chechen capital, Grozny.
He blamed the attacks on Russian "special services", implying they had an interest in causing problems in relations between Moscow and Chechnya.

Chechen leaders are still demanding full independence for their mainly Moslem region, despite last August's ceasefire which ended fighting that killed tens of thousands of people. Moscow has ruled out secession.

Radical Chechen guerrilla commander Salman Raduyev has vowed to attack Russia's rail network and other targets to press the campaign for independence and to avenge independence leader Dzhokhar Dudayev's death in a Russian rocket attack.
Tass said Raduyev had claimed responsibility for last week's explosion at Armavir, but more moderate Chechen leaders said they doubted he was behind the attack.
